environment.description: Same container image deployed on Ubuntu 22.04 host with AppArmor profile 'ws-realtime-confined' loaded and enforced. The profile was generated via aa-genprof during a training run and then manually tightened. Profile allows write ONLY to /var/log/websocket-service/messages.log (exact path match, no globbing) and denies link, rename, and mount operations. Additionally, the profile includes a 'deny /var/log/websocket-service/** w' rule that prevents creation of NEW files in the log directory (only the pre-existing messages.log is writable). The profile also sets 'deny /proc/*/mem rw' and 'deny /sys/** w'. The Fluentd sidecar in this environment runs with a SEPARATE AppArmor profile that restricts its read access to only /var/log/websocket-service/messages.log and denies network egress except to the internal Elasticsearch endpoint on port 9200. Note: the ws-realtime-confined profile does NOT sanitize log content — it only restricts file operations.

config.fluentd_apparmor: fluentd-confined (read only messages.log, egress only to ES:9200)
config.filesystem: read-only rootfs except explicit AppArmor allows
